proposed.explanation:
Your friend's numbers are wrong on both counts. The FY2025 net profit is 22,578,063,000 EGP (≈ 22.58 billion), not 225.9 billion – the friend likely misread the thousands-unit figure. And the 2024 profit was 10,111,328,000 EGP, so 2025 is about 2.2× the prior year, not more than ten times. Revenue also grew a solid ~31 % (81.68 bn → 106.67 bn), and EPS rose from 4.79 to 11.93 EGP/share. Total equity expanded from 45.94 bn to 63.69 bn, indicating the company is retaining and compounding earnings.

That said, putting ALL 50,000 EGP into ETEL is not advisable for two reasons. First, the diversification rule caps any single holding at 50 % of total portfolio value. Your portfolio is worth 71,292.50 EGP (50,000 cash + 150 × 141.95), so ETEL can be at most 35,646.25 EGP. You already hold 21,292.50 EGP in ETEL, leaving room for at most 14,353.75 EGP of additional shares, i.e. 101 shares (101 × 141.95 = 14,336.95 EGP). After the buy, ETEL would be 251 shares worth 35,629.45 EGP – 49.98 % of the portfolio – and you would keep 35,663.05 EGP in cash.

Second, you only have two years of results. The 123 % profit jump is impressive, but a single year of growth does not guarantee a repeat, and I have no dividend data, forward guidance, or sector-competitive context in the evidence. With a 5-year retirement horizon and medium risk tolerance, a moderate add-on to a fundamentally improving telecom is reasonable, but concentrating 100 % of your liquid assets in one stock would be too risky.

Risks to keep in mind: telecom is a regulated, capital-intensive sector; the 2025 profit surge could partly reflect one-off items not visible in the summary figures; and the share price of 141.95 EGP implies a P/E of roughly 11.9× on 2025 EPS, which is fair but not a deep value. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
